subtitle: The common caliper, different behaviour
description: A direct-applied cartridge variant of the disc concept for controlled process braking. Loss of actuation releases braking force; it does not inherit spring-applied holding behaviour.
targets: Must be acceptable to the machine safety concept
decisions: Reuse the rotor and selected metalwork only after confirming actuator loads.
Keep the operating principle explicit to prevent selection as a default holding brake.
Buy direct-actuation cylinders and define modulation requirements separately.
materials: Shared concept bridge/pad materials with AB-DC.
Direct actuator: supplier-selected seals, body and piston materials.
risks: No modulation loop, thermal-duty capability or emergency-stop approval.
steps: Confirm application permits loss of braking on loss of supply.
Assemble shared caliper metalwork and supplier direct actuators.
Set pressure limiting and independent protection after system review.
hypotheses: Measure released BOM reuse with AB-DC.
Measure torque tracking after actuator and controller selection.
sensors: Advisory position / wear sensing with replaceable brackets; no AI-controlled brake release.
Record supplier sensor range, supply, connector, EMC, ingress and temperature limits before selection.
Define independent machine safety interface and diagnostic fault response with the responsible controls engineer.
